title: The Letter Opener
brief:
A dinner at the family's country house, rain against the windows. Shortly after 20:25, Clara is found dead in the library, killed with the letter opener from her own desk. Apart from her, only two people were in the house that evening: her niece Anna and her business partner Ben.

Find out who is responsible for Clara's death. Search the library and the garden, examine what you find, and question Anna and Ben. Not every lead points to the culprit, and silence is not yet a confession.
challengeQuestion: Who is responsible for Clara's death?

labels.label: Anna
labels.role: the lady of the house's niece

publicRules.text: What a found item itself shows counts as fact. Statements made by people can be mistaken.
Anyone who was in the Garden at 20:25 was not involved in Clara's death and is not responsible.
Apart from Clara, exactly one person was present at her death. Whoever was present is responsible.

epilogue:
Ben breaks down. “She wanted to ruin me,” he says, his voice failing. He owed Clara money he could not pay back, and that evening the two of them argued in the library about the will. At 20:25 he reached for the letter opener on the desk. Under questioning he lied: he had not been there, Anna had done it.

Anna had nothing to do with Clara's death. She was working in the garden at the time, her gloves covered in fresh soil. Her fingerprint on the handle of the letter opener was a false lead: she had used it to open letters in the afternoon.
